title: Crowd Coach: Peer Coaching for Crowd Workers’ Skill Growth
venue: Proceedings of the ACM on Human-Computer Interaction
extended_summary:
This paper addresses how to support skill development for crowd workers without relying on expert mentors or requesters. The authors argue that crowd work platforms like Amazon Mechanical Turk do not naturally support workers’ learning and advancement, even though workers want to improve their speed and quality over time. To address this, they designed Crowd Coach, a Chrome extension that lets workers both give and receive very short peer coaching snippets while completing tasks.

The system has two main parts: Micro-Coaching, which lets workers submit brief advice for specific task types, and Selective Coaching, which ranks coaching snippets using peer assessments so workers see advice others found useful. The study focuses on crowd workers doing AMT tasks, especially novice workers doing audio transcription. The controlled field experiment compared three conditions: no coaching, random coaching snippets, and selected peer coaching via Crowd Coach. Participants were 90 novice AMT workers randomly assigned to conditions.

Results showed that workers receiving selected peer coaching completed audio transcription tasks significantly faster than those in the control or random-coaching conditions, while accuracy did not significantly differ. A deployment study with 179 installed users further showed that workers actively used the system across many task types and generally found it useful. The paper concludes that lightweight peer coaching can improve worker speed without hurting quality and may support informal on-the-job skill growth in crowd work.

identified_tools.name: Crowd Coach
identified_tools.description: A browser plugin / crowd-work system that provides peer micro-coaching snippets to workers while they are completing tasks, with voting-based selection of higher-quality advice.
identified_tools.use_case: Studied as an on-the-job peer coaching tool for AMT workers, compared against no coaching and random coaching snippets in a controlled field experiment, and also examined in a real-world deployment.

findings.finding_summary: In a controlled field experiment with 90 novice AMT workers, Crowd Coach was compared with a no-coaching control and a random-coaching condition on audio transcription tasks. The paper reports significant differences across conditions for task accuracy and completion time (MANOVA F(2,74)=17.53, p<0.0001); completion time was significantly lower in the Crowd Coach condition (M=184.1, SD=12.36) than control (M=262.79, SD=37.38) and random coaching (M=284.21, SD=46.44), while accuracy was not significantly different (F(2,74)=2.47, p=.09).
findings.measure: Audio transcription completion time and word error rate / accuracy
findings.sample_size: n=90 (26 control, 26 random coaching, 25 Crowd Coach completed all tasks)

quality_tier_rationale: This is a controlled field experiment with random assignment and a real-world deployment, which provides stronger evidence than purely qualitative work. However, it is not a K-12 education study and the outcome is task performance in crowd work rather than teacher learning, so the overall evidence is moderately strong but context-limited.
impact_tier_rationale: The intervention produced a clear reduction in completion time in the experimental condition, with no measurable loss in accuracy. That suggests a modest-to-medium practical effect on worker efficiency, though it does not speak to teacher practice or student learning.
